text: Within 24 hours of your last cigarette, the carbon monoxide level in your blood returns to normal.
After just two days, nerve endings begin to regrow and your senses of taste and smell start to sharpen.
Two to twelve weeks in, your circulation improves and physical activity becomes noticeably easier.
By nine months, the cilia in your lungs have largely recovered, cutting coughing and infections.
After one year smoke-free, your excess risk of coronary heart disease is about half that of a smoker.
Every craving you ride out rewires the habit loop a little more — urges peak and pass in just a few minutes.
